day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 4:00 PM. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA via Condor flight at 16:00. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Settle into your room, freshen up, and get oriented with a quick walk around the immediate hotel area.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short drive or rideshare to Historic Downtown Rome for a relaxed first-evening stroll. Enjoy the charming streetscapes, browse shop windows, and soak in the small-city atmosphere along Broad Street. Keep it light since it's an arrival day.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight or airport meal before arrival.
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight or airport meal before arrival.
meals.dinner: Harvest Moon Café (Downtown Rome) – A local favorite with affordable Southern-inspired dishes. Expect $10–$16 per person. Alternatively, grab a budget-friendly bite at Mellow Mushroom on Broad Street (~$10–$14).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very relaxed. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Download a local map or rideshare app (Uber/Lyft) as public transit in Rome, GA is limited. Average high is ~30°C, so stay hydrated and pack light breathable clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Start with the Rome, GA Historic Downtown Art Walk. Spend 2–3 hours exploring vibrant murals, local galleries, and public art installations scattered throughout downtown. Begin at the Rome Area Council for the Arts and work your way along Broad Street and surrounding blocks. This is free and self-guided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring downtown – visit the Clock Tower atop Neely Hill for a panoramic view of the three rivers (free, short hike). Then head to the Rome Area History Museum for a low-cost deep dive into local heritage (~$5 entry). Browse the gift shop for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest during the hottest part of the late afternoon, then head back downtown for dinner and a relaxed evening walk along the Oostanaula River waterfront.

meals.breakfast: La Quinta complimentary breakfast (included with most La Quinta stays – confirm at check-in). Enjoy eggs, waffles, and coffee at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Partridge Café or a local deli in downtown Rome – budget sandwiches and wraps for $8–$12.
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant, Rome – generous portions at very affordable prices, $9–$14 per person. Great for budget travelers.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a refillable water bottle. The Art Walk is entirely free. Start the morning walk before 10 AM to beat the heat (highs near 30°C). Sunscreen is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or rideshare (~10 minutes from the hotel) to the Chieftains Museum & Major Ridge Home Tour. Spend the morning exploring this National Historic Landmark, learning about Cherokee history, the Trail of Tears, and the life of Major Ridge. Entry is typically $8–$10 per adult – very budget-friendly for the depth of history offered.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, head to the nearby Coosa Valley Farmers Market (if open – check local schedule) for fresh local produce and artisan snacks. Then visit the Forum River Center area for free outdoor art and river views. Relax by the confluence of the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local food scene in downtown Rome. Check if any free Friday evening events or live music are happening at the Forum or local venues – Rome often hosts community events in summer.

meals.breakfast: La Quinta complimentary breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Grab fresh fruit, local cheese, and baked goods from the Farmers Market for a picnic by the river – budget $6–$10.
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli, Rome – a beloved local spot with hearty sandwiches and comfort food at $10–$15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Chieftains Museum hours are typically Tuesday–Saturday; confirm hours before visiting. The museum is only a short distance from the hotel on Riverside Parkway, making it very convenient. Bring cash for the farmers market.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Berry College Campus for the Art & Nature Walk. Explore the stunning Gothic architecture, on-campus art collections, and scenic natural landscapes. The campus is one of the largest in the world by acreage and is free to walk. Look for the historic Ford Buildings and the beautiful Mill area. Start early (8–9 AM) to enjoy cooler temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Berry College – visit the campus art gallery and walk the nature trails. Keep an eye out for the resident deer herd, a beloved campus attraction. Pack a light snack and enjoy the shaded trails. This is a full half-day experience easily.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel, shower and refresh, then head to downtown Rome for a Saturday evening out. Browse local boutiques and enjoy the livelier weekend atmosphere on Broad Street.

meals.breakfast: La Quinta complimentary breakfast – fuel up before the nature walk.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local grocery store (Kroger or Walmart near the hotel) – sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for under $8 total.
meals.dinner: DaVinci's Pizzeria, Rome – excellent wood-fired pizza at budget-friendly prices, $10–$15 per person. A local favorite on weekends.

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is about 5–10 minutes from the hotel by car. Wear sturdy walking shoes for the nature trails. Bring insect repellent for wooded trail sections. The campus is open to the public but respect academic and residential areas.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit your favorite art spots from the Downtown Art Walk for any murals or galleries you may have missed. Many local galleries have rotating exhibits – check if any new shows opened over the weekend. Visit the Broad Street Arts District at a leisurely Sunday pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to nearby Cave Spring, GA (~20 minutes from Rome) – a charming small town with a natural limestone cave (Rolater Park Cave, ~$3 entry), a natural spring, and a beautiful park with a swimming pool. Great for a hot afternoon dip (pool entry ~$3–$5).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a quiet Sunday evening. Pick up groceries and cook a simple meal in the hotel room (if kitchenette available) or opt for a casual takeout dinner to save on budget.

meals.breakfast: La Quinta complimentary breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Rolater Park in Cave Spring – bring packed food from the hotel area grocery store. Budget $6–$8.
meals.dinner: Takeout from Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near the hotel on Chateau Drive – quick, affordable, $7–$10 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a hidden gem and very budget-friendly. Bring a swimsuit for the pool at Rolater Park. Sunday hours for some attractions may be limited – call ahead. This is a great low-key day to recharge mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning doing a deeper food-focused exploration of Rome. Visit a local bakery or coffee shop for a leisurely breakfast, then explore the Rome area's food culture – check out any local specialty food shops, hot sauce makers, or artisan producers in the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Etowah Indian Mounds State Historic Site (~45 minutes from Rome in Cartersville, GA) – a fascinating archaeological site with ancient Native American earthwork mounds, a museum, and river views. Entry is ~$7 per adult. Pairs well with the Cherokee history learned at Chieftains Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a final evening exploration. Walk the Riverwalk trail along the Oostanaula River at sunset – completely free and beautiful in the golden evening light.

meals.breakfast: Harvest Moon Café or a local Rome bakery – treat yourself to a proper sit-down breakfast, $8–$12.
meals.lunch: On-site or nearby the Etowah Mounds – pack a lunch or stop at a local diner in Cartersville for $8–$12.
meals.dinner: Pastime Restaurant, Rome – a classic local diner with Southern comfort food at very affordable prices, $9–$14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Etowah Indian Mounds is a worthwhile day trip that complements the Cherokee history theme of the trip. Confirm Monday opening hours before departing. The mounds involve some climbing – wear good shoes and bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – take one last walk through Historic Downtown to pick up any souvenirs from local art galleries or boutiques. Look for affordable prints or postcards from local artists as budget-friendly mementos. Visit any gallery or spot you want to see one more time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (standard checkout is 11 AM – confirm with hotel). If your departure is later, store luggage at the front desk. Spend remaining time at a local café or riverside park. Reflect on the trip over a final local meal.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome, GA. Head to the airport or onward destination. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: La Quinta complimentary breakfast – last chance to enjoy the free hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Broad Street Baking Company or a downtown café – a farewell lunch with local flavor, $9–$13.
meals.dinner: Airport or travel meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Pack the night before to make checkout smooth. Rome, GA does not have a major commercial airport – the nearest major airports are Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International (~75 miles south) or Chattanooga Metropolitan (~75 miles north). Plan transport accordingly. Keep receipts for any art purchases for insurance or customs purposes.

Chat with vendors, pick up snacks for the day, and soak in the community atmosphere. The market typically runs Friday mornings.

Visit a local cooking-focused shop or take a self-guided food tour sampling Southern cuisine staples: boiled peanuts, peach preserves, local honey, and artisan cheeses picked up at the market or nearby specialty shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sit-down farm-to-table dinner at one of Rome's celebrated local restaurants. Treat yourself slightly – this is your dedicated food-focused evening. Pair your meal with a local craft beer or Georgia wine.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Farmers Market itself – fresh fruit, baked goods, and local coffee from market vendors. ~$8–$15.
meals.lunch: Light picnic-style lunch using market finds (cheese, bread, fruit, preserves) enjoyed at a nearby park or the Riverwalk. ~$10–$15.
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual farm-to-table restaurant on Broad Street. Budget ~$30–$45 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the Coosa Valley Farmers Market schedule ahead of time – hours and location can vary seasonally. Bring a reusable bag for market purchases. Friday evenings in downtown Rome can be lively, so reservations for dinner are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Berry College Campus Art & Nature Walk – Drive approximately 10–15 minutes from the hotel to Berry College. Explore the stunning Gothic architecture, on-campus art collections, and scenic natural landscapes. The campus is one of the largest in the world by acreage and is beautiful in early summer. Look for the resident deer herd near the mill area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Berry College's trails and outdoor spaces, or visit the college's historic Old Mill and Ford Buildings. Alternatively, head back toward Rome and visit Myrtle Hill Cemetery for panoramic views of the city and the confluence of the three rivers – a hidden gem for art and history lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in Downtown Rome – explore the local nightlife scene with live music venues or a relaxed dinner. Check local event listings for any weekend art openings or outdoor performances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bakery/café near Chateau Drive. ~$8–$12.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or stop at a café near Berry College. Alternatively, return to Rome for lunch at a Broad Street spot. ~$12–$18.
meals.dinner: Casual Saturday dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant – try something with a Southern BBQ or Tex-Mex flair for variety. ~$20–$28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is free to visit and open to the public. Wear comfortable shoes for walking on uneven terrain. Bring water and sunscreen. Saturday is a great day to check local event boards (Rome's Facebook community pages or the Rome News-Tribune events section) for pop-up art shows or food events.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning – sleep in or enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit a local Rome brunch spot to experience the Sunday brunch culture. Afterward, revisit any Downtown art galleries or murals you may have missed earlier in the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Rome Area History Museum or take a self-guided architectural walking tour of Rome's historic neighborhoods, admiring the Victorian and antebellum homes. Pick up a walking tour map from the Rome Welcome Center on Broad Street.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset picnic or outdoor dining – pick up provisions from a local market or deli and head to the Rome Riverwalk or Ridge Ferry Park for a relaxed outdoor evening meal as the sun sets over the Coosa River.

meals.breakfast: Sunday brunch at a local café – try eggs Benedict, shrimp and grits, or a Southern brunch plate. ~$15–$22.
meals.lunch: Light snack or skip in favor of a larger brunch.
meals.dinner: Picnic at Ridge Ferry Park with deli provisions, or a casual dinner at a Broad Street restaurant. ~$15–$25.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday hours for museums and galleries may be limited – check ahead. This is a good day to recharge before the final stretch of the trip. The Riverwalk is free and beautiful at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Historic Downtown Art Walk for a deeper exploration – revisit favorite murals or discover new ones. Visit any galleries you haven't yet entered. Consider purchasing a piece of local art as a souvenir – many galleries offer affordable prints and small works.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip or extended exploration: Drive to nearby Cave Spring (~15 miles southwest of Rome) to visit the charming historic village, the natural cave, and the artisan shops. This small town has a strong arts and crafts community and is a lovely half-day excursion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for your final full evening dinner. Choose your favorite restaurant from the week for a repeat visit, or try somewhere new you've been curious about.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a downtown Rome café. ~$8–$12.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Cave Spring at a local diner or café – budget-friendly Southern cooking. ~$10–$16.
meals.dinner: Celebratory final full-day dinner at your top pick from the week. ~$25–$40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a short, scenic drive and worth the detour for art and food lovers. The cave and pool in Cave Spring are a fun stop if temperatures are high. Monday can be quieter at most venues, which is ideal for a more personal gallery experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – enjoy a leisurely breakfast and pack up. Take one last walk along the Riverwalk or through Downtown to say goodbye to the city. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs, local food products (jams, honey, pecans), or art pieces from Broad Street shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit any remaining items on your list – the Chieftains Museum gift shop, a final gallery, or simply relax at the hotel pool before checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome, GA. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Full sit-down farewell breakfast at a local diner – biscuits, gravy, eggs, and coffee. ~$10–$16.
meals.lunch: Light lunch or grab-and-go from a Broad Street café before heading to the airport or continuing your journey. ~$10–$15.
meals.dinner: In transit / at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00 AM – 12:00 PM). Keep luggage stored at the hotel if your departure is later in the day. Confirm any return flight or onward travel arrangements the night before. Rome, GA is a small, walkable city – a wonderful hidden gem for art and food lovers.
